- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., spikes above 75–80) — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such events.  
- Model overestimates downward moves (e.g., drops below 65–68) — adjust downward by 2–5% for such events.  
- Forecast shows gradual, flat trend but true outcome has strong mean reversion — apply slight downward bias after peak or sudden drop.  
- If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early reversal, reduce forecast slope slightly to account for sentiment-driven correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 2–5 days — adjust forecast to anticipate 1–2 days ahead of actual turn.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive spikes (e.g., 0.20), model tends to ignore them — amplify small sentiment-driven corrections.
